command.name: security key-manager external azure enable
command.description: This command is deprecated and may be removed in a future release. Use the security key-manager external azure create-config command to create an Azure Key Vault configuration and the security key-manager keystore enable command to enable it instead. This command enables the Azure Key Vault (AKV) associated with the given Vserver and creates a configuration with the name "default". An Azure application and an AKV must be deployed on the Azure portal prior to running this command. This command is not supported for the admin Vserver, or if a key manager for the given data Vserver is already enabled. This command is also not supported in a MetroCluster environment.

parameter.name: vserver
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the Vserver on which the AKV is to be enabled.

parameter.name: authentication-method
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify either client_secret authentication or certificate authentication for the deployed AKV.

parameter.name: client-id
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the client (application) ID of the deployed Azure application.

parameter.name: tenant-id
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the tenant (directory) ID of the deployed Azure application.

parameter.name: name
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the DNS name of the deployed AKV.

parameter.name: key-id
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the key identifier of the AKV Key Encryption Key (KEK).

parameter.name: oauth-host
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the host name of the Open Authorization server.

parameter.name: port
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the port of the deployed AKV.

parameter.name: verify
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify whether to verify the identity of AKV.

parameter.name: verify-host
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify whether to verify the identity of AKV hostname.

parameter.name: verify-ip
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify whether to verify the identity of AKV ip address.

parameter.name: proxy-type
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the proxy type.

parameter.name: proxy-host
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the proxy hostname.

parameter.name: proxy-port
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the proxy port.

parameter.name: proxy-username
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the proxy username.

parameter.name: proxy-password
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the proxy password.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the AKV connection timeout in seconds.

parameter.name: vault-host
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the AKV vault host.

parameter.name: polling-period
parameter.description: Use this parameter to specify the AKV polling period in seconds.

example.p: The following example enables the AKV for Vserver v1. An Azure application with client-id "4a0f9c98-c5aa-4275-abe3-2780cf2801c3", tenant-id "8e21f23a-10b9-46fb-9d50-720ef604be98", client secret (not echoed to the screen for security purposes), OAuth host at 10.12.34.1 and an AKV with DNS name "https://akv-keyvault.vault.azure.net" is deployed on the Azure portal. An AKV KEK with DNS name "https://akv-keyvault.vault.azure.net/keys/key1/a8e619fd8f234db3b0b95c59540e2a74" is created on the Azure portal for the AKV.
example.screen:
cluster-1::>security key-manager external azure enable -client-id 4a0f9c98-c5aa-4275-abe3-2780cf2801c3 -tenant-id 8e21f23a-10b9-46fb-9d50-720ef604be98 -name https://akv-keyvault.vault.azure.net -key-id https://akv-keyvault.vault.azure.net/keys/key1/a8e619fd8f234db3b0b95c59540e2a74 -authentication-method client_secret -vserver v1 -oauth-host 10.12.34.1
